title: The Army Trained Pigeons to Steer Missiles #shorts

lines.text: During World War Two, a famous psychologist tried to put pigeons inside a missile, so they could steer it.
His name was B. F. Skinner. He trained pigeons to peck at a picture of a target, and every peck earned them grain.
Inside the nose cone, three pigeons watched a screen. When they pecked the target, the missile turned toward it.
The government gave him twenty five thousand dollars. The birds passed the tests, but officials thought the idea was too crazy, and shut it down.
Skinner kept the pigeons, and years later they still pecked perfectly.
The Navy revived it as Project Orcon, until electronics replaced the birds. So, would you trust a pigeon with a missile?

sources: https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smithsonian-institution/bf-skinners-pigeon-guided-rocket-53443995/ (started ~1943; NDRC gave Skinner $25,000; three pigeons in nose cone peck at projected image on three screens; officials stayed skeptical and ended project; pigeons still pecking strongly 1, 2, 4, 6 years later)

https://www.army.mil/article/111511/its_a_bird_its_a_plane (pigeons trained with grain; no washouts in class of 64; never used in combat; renamed Project Orcon for the Navy after the war; Orcon cancelled 1953 when electronic guidance proved reliable)
